articles.title: Türk warns of widening risk of atrocity crimes against Palestinians
articles.summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Wednesday warned of a widening risk of further atrocity crimes by Israel against Palestinians, saying violence in the occupied West Bank in recent months has heightened existential fears.

articles.title: World News in Brief: Vaccine crisis in Yemen, aid for Ukraine, another UNRWA staffer killed
articles.summary: More than 364,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since the beginning of August as fighting and insecurity continue, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Gaza war has undone 77 years of human development, UN warns
articles.summary: The UN deputy chief urged renewed international support for a two-State solution to the Israel-Palestine conflict on Monday, warning that Palestinians continue to face violence, displacement and dire living conditions despite the October 2025 ceasefire in Gaza.

articles.title: Guterres laments COP31 outcome, urges climate justice from Barbados
articles.summary: Secretary-General António Guterres on Sunday expressed deep disappointment over the collapse of COP31 climate negotiations, using a visit to Barbados to call for stronger action on fossil fuels, climate finance and support for vulnerable nations.

articles.title: ‘We escaped with only our lives’: Fighting to give birth in war-torn Yemen
articles.summary: When fighting suddenly escalated around Taiz, in southwestern Yemen two months ago, midwife Anisa Fadhl had no time to pack a bag before she fled, leaving behind her home and her clinic. Both were later looted and destroyed.

articles.title: Bridgetown AI summit to tackle safety as risks outpace capacity to respond
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres is heading to Barbados to co-host a special summit on artificial intelligence (AI) safety on Monday, aimed at closing the gap between accelerating risks and many countries’ capacity to deal with the pace of development.

articles.title: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns
articles.summary: From aid convoys in conflict zones to passenger jets and cargo ships far out at sea, safe journeys depend on GPS, satellite navigation and old-fashioned radio transmissions. But these signals are increasingly being blocked or faked – and civilians are paying the price.
